items.title: De De Pierce Interview, 1960-01-10
items.q: But Chris was just actually anywhere, any little job, three pieces, four pieces, he would get to play it.

ctx.x: Chris? Yeah. Didn't you say something about brother and Guy there?

Oh, they were two brothers, yeah, quite natural. But Guy Kelly, yeah, oh yeah, they were brothers. But Guy Kelly was more musical, you know, reading man. Read more. That's how he stayed more with Papa Celestine. But Chris was just actually anywhere, any little job, three pieces, four pieces, he would get to play it. But they claim he knew a lot of music. He never played it though. I was told he read red, red, yeah, red, nice. He got out of the story. What about this fella, Rochon, you mentioned
the other day? Alexis. Is that his name, Alexis Rochon? Alexis Rochon. And what instrument did he play?

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02
items.q: Of course I played alongside him a long time, off and on, different jobs, he'd hire me.

ctx.x: Okay, we got it going again. You're talking about Mr. Chris Kelly?

Chris Kelly, yeah. He was known as one of the greatest blues players that I ever known. It was known, it has been proven, that Chris Kelly, as though he was playing a dance, he could play a blues and otherwise start a general fight over the music, the blues, and break up a dance. He'd known he could do that, make disagreement among the dancers. He played those blues, it was such a feeling. He got people to go to fight in the place. He was known for that. Strictly a blues man. Of course I played alongside him a…
Did he use a lot of mutes?

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07
items.q: Yeah, he worked a lot of blues. I wish he was a blues man, you know.

ctx.x: What about Chris Kelly? Do you think he had any influence on you?

Yeah, he worked a lot of blues. I wish he was a blues man, you know. Uh huh. Do you know his blues today, any of them? Oh, it's so many. It's another thing. He played so much with himself. Careless, love, and all those other numbers like that.
Oh yeah, he'll be, he'll be. Uh, did you have any other teachers besides Rene and Charlene?
